 NBC’s Sunday Night Football broadcast omits national anthem at Soldier Field
 Monday, 9 November 2026, 14:15 
 Photo source: Fox News 
 NBC did not air the national anthem before Sunday night’s game at Soldier Field, during the NFL’s Salute to Service week and three days before Veterans Day. 
 After introducing analysts Cris Collinsworth and Noah Eagle, NBC aired a pregame interview with Bears quarterback Caleb Williams. An aerial shot then showed flag bearers carrying a folded, field-sized American flag back into a stadium tunnel. The broadcast did not include the national anthem. It did air the “show anthem” featuring Carrie Underwood and cover the trade of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears.
 This is reported by Fox News .
 OutKick contacted NBC executive vice president of communications Greg Hughes and senior vice president of communications Chris McCloskey to ask why the anthem was omitted. Neither had responded by publication time. Some viewers also noted the absence on social media. The report says the decision to air the anthem is generally made by the network, not the NFL or a club, and describes the omission as apparently an editorial decision by NBC.
 Advertisement 
 The report also points to an earlier anthem-related incident before a Bears game this season. On September 28, Mariachi Herencia de Mexico performed an instrumental mariachi version of “The Star-Spangled Banner” at Soldier Field before the Bears’ Monday Night Football game on ESPN/ABC, as part of the team’s Hispanic Heritage Month “Vamos Bears” celebration. Reactions to the performance were mixed. Caleb Williams, who was injured, was shown pacing along the sideline while the anthem played. The report speculates that NBC may have wanted to avoid offending anyone by not airing the anthem, adding that the decision did not work.
